title: Four separate authority questions
summary: Job placement, outbound egress, web-application interaction and observation are deliberately separate planes even though they reuse identity, proofs, generations, sessions and leases.
invariants: Job-to-Node Allocation answers where a job may and can execute; it does not reserve API egress sessions.
API Client answers how an outbound operation may leave the environment; it does not place the owning job.
Virtual Browser answers how a web application is interacted with semantically; it does not own node placement or network routing authority.
Observation answers what an interactive engine currently exposes to an observer; observation authority never implies control authority.
Similar mechanisms do not justify merging materially different authority questions into one scheduler or one lease type.

provenance.claim: Allocator explicitly composes general placement with later API Client route/session reservation.
Virtual Browser preserves browser/API/placement boundaries and leaves outbound authority to API Client.
Observation is a neutral read-only service with external authority seam.
